observations: What I read: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (supplied as project instructions); all of docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md and docs/PROMPTS.md; the whole prepared request, including the decision, dialoguePolicy, dialogueInstructions and all 23 panels; all of source/original.txt; all of workflow/source-coverage.json; and script-all-r8.json for context. Every file was readable. I first read only the lettered strings in panel order, then compared them with the source. To check continuity I opened these accepted panel PNGs with Read: 03-2, 03-3, 03-4, 05-1, 05-3 and 05-4. This does not certify any artwork. This is a script request, so the first-reading step with unnumbered images does not apply.

Lettering: every dialogue, caption and label string matches the source word for word, and each panel's textColumns join back into its text. The only split is 01-2, where one Meera line becomes two balloons by the same speaker with no one speaking in between. No turns are merged across another speaker. Each question is answered in the next panel: 03-1>03-2, 03-2>03-3, 04-1>04-2 and 05-2>05-3. Every referent appears before it is used: 'the rest' (01-3), 'here' (02-2), 'And our team' (02-3), 'your concerns' (04-4) and 'That's the idea' (05-3). The voices fit: Ananya calm, Meera polite, Ravi casual. Each product has one role and one carrier: Practice on the laptop (02-1), Care on the staff phone (02-3), Health on Ravi's own phone (05-2). The vision is kept separate: only 06-2 and 06-3 carry the WELBUK VISION label and vignette, and 06-1 keeps 'may'. No medical claims, real data or invented features.

Fix 1 is verified. 03-2 now records ravi-phone with heldBy ravi.right, and the hands entry names ravi-phone. In the image, Ravi is seen from behind on the left, facing right, and the phone is in the hand on the far side of his torso, which reads as his right hand. 03-3 records the phone lying on the desk with heldBy none, and the image shows a dark blue phone on the desk in front of him while both his hands rest on the desk edge. 05-1 now gives the history 'carried by Ravi since registration (put away during the consultation)', and production.before says 'took his phone out again'. In the 05-1 image the phone is in the hand without the watch (his right), and the hand wearing the watch rests on the desk. The 03-2 to 05-1 history is now consistent.

Fix 2 is verified. 05-3 records the phone as 'held in Ravi's left hand in the foreground' with heldBy ravi.left. In the image, the hand holding the phone at foreground right wears the wristwatch, which is consistent with Ravi's left wrist.

Fix 3 is verified. sections.departure.costumes now lists Ananya (teal kurta, open white coat, stethoscope not in use), Meera (blue kurta, white churidar, silver bangle) and Ravi. The 05-4 image matches: Ananya waves with her right hand and Meera with her left from the doorway, and Ravi waves with his right hand while holding the phone in his left, the hand with the watch.

Not blocking, record wording only: (a) 03-4 has no ravi-phone entry, and Ravi's hands are on the bag strap and empty, while 03-3's after says 'picked up again after registration'. In the 03-4 image no phone is visible, so the phone is implicitly put away, which fits 05-1's 'carried since registration'. An optional note could say 'pocketed'. (b) 05-2 lists heldBy ravi.right although the phone is held in both hands. A single heldBy value is acceptable. (c) Some scene text is now stale: 03-2 still calls Ravi 'off-panel left' and 01-3 calls the desk off-panel, although both are now partly visible. Later artwork and storyboard reviews can confirm this. None of these points needs new artwork or changes the reading.

panels.observation: The source caption is kept word for word. It names Ananya and sets up the 'busy' premise that Meera's complaint in 01-2 depends on.
Meera's single source line is split at the ellipsis into two balloons by the same speaker, with nothing in between. The list gives 'everything' its referent.
Ananya's line is word for word. 'the rest' refers back to the 01-2 list, and Meera, still mid-call in the background, motivates her decision.
The onboarding caption is word for word, with evening light marking the time change. The Practice label names the source's 'laptop view of Welbuk Practice' without claiming any feature.
The line is word for word. 'here' refers to the laptop introduced in 02-1, and her considering team roles leads into Meera's line.
'And our team...' is word for word and continues 02-2 with no other speaker between them. The Care label matches the source's 'staff phone displaying Welbuk Care'.
'One team. Better coordination.' is word for word and sums up 02-2 and 02-3. Meera's silent nod is an added reaction, not a dropped line.
Ravi's greeting and request are word for word, addressed to Meera at the desk. 'Of course' in 03-2 answers his request.
The line is word for word. It answers 03-1 and asks the consent question that 03-3 replies to. The ravi-phone prop is now recorded as heldBy ravi.right, which matches the image.
'Yes, please.' answers the 03-2 consent question. The monitor shows blank fields only, matching 'no actual identifying data'. The phone lying on the desk is recorded with heldBy none.
'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' is word for word. His name follows from the registration, and the gesture toward the chairs leads into page 4.
The greeting is word for word. 'Tell me what brings you in' is the question 04-2 answers, and the same costumes show it is the same visit.
'I've been feeling tired lately.' answers 04-1 word for word as a routine concern with no diagnosis.
The caption is word for word, backed by a silent attentive listener and the closed laptop. The Ananya-left / Ravi-right sides are kept.
The line is word for word. 'your concerns' refers back to 04-2, with no instruments in use and no treatment advice.
Meera's line is word for word and keeps the careful 'designed to help'. The phone history now runs consistently from 03-2 and 03-3 ('took his phone out again').
Ravi's question is word for word and depends on Meera's explanation in 05-1. The abstract cards stand in for the source's 'appointments and health information' without showing any data.
'That's the idea' answers 05-2, and 'what is available to you' is kept word for word, so no unlaunched feature is implied. The phone is now recorded as heldBy ravi.left, which matches the image.
The caption is word for word. The doorway send-off follows the walkthrough, and the departure costumes now cover all three visible characters.
The caption is word for word and keeps the conditional 'may'. The non-vision train panel carries the change of time and place.
The 'WELBUK VISION' label the source asks for and the caption are word for word inside the vignette. Nothing suggests a launched referral feature.
The caption is word for word. The repeated vision label and the vignette keep the family wellness app conceptual.
The three product labels and the final caption are word for word. The present-day group ties Practice, Care and Health back to 02-1, 02-3 and 05-2.
